subject: Private maintenance safety-lane: pinning, canary & audit plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Gloria Chen <gloria.chen@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Ops <ops+prod@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Private maintenance safety-lane: initial proposal and ask

Hi Gloria / Acme ops team,

We'd like to propose a short maintenance window for your Private deployment so we can apply the November security patches, runtime kernel updates, and the new kv-cache invalidation guard that improves pin-resilience. High-level proposal:

- Proposed window: 2026-11-27 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (low traffic window)
- Scope: control-plane patching, agent-side runtime update (no model topology changes), canary subset (10% of pods), then fleet ramp
- Expected user impact: negligible; per-pod restart expected <5 minutes during rolling canary.
- Pinning policy: we recommend a temporary pin to current stable revision for 72 hours post-rollout with automatic unpin after health checks pass.

Attachments: maintenance-plan-outline.pdf (high level schedule + rollback triggers)

Questions for you:
1) Does the proposed window conflict with any batch jobs or reporting at your side?
2) Do you need additional audit logs / KMS access for your compliance review?
3) Any constraints around permanent IP changes or firewall maintenance windows?

If this window works, we will follow up with a detailed runbook (canary steps, telemetry gates, rollback checklist) and a short readiness call next week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Redwood Inference | hosting/private inference for production LLM workloads

From: Gloria Chen <gloria.chen@acmehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:07:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Private maintenance safety-lane: initial proposal and ask

Jordan, thanks for the heads up. A couple of notes from our side:

- The proposed UTC window on 11/27 is generally acceptable, but we have a reporting job that starts 04:30 UTC and runs until ~05:15 UTC. Can we avoid touching any pods that serve that job during the hourly run?
- We need detail on the "pinning for 72 hours" approach. Our compliance team wants to understand the exact rollback timeline and whether you keep audit-level diffs of binaries/versions.
- SOC2 evidence: please include the up-to-date SOC 2 control map and the audit trail for any KMS operations that touch customer keys during the maintenance.

Also looping in procurement to confirm whether a change order is required for out-of-hours operations.

Gloria Chen
Director, Platform Operations
AcmeHealth

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:14:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Private maintenance safety-lane: internal ops proposal

Team — internal draft to address Gloria's asks and to lock the operational plan. I'll run the canary and telemetry gating. Key items below:

Canary & Rollout
- Canary slice: 10% of customer pods in one AZ (non-primary past-traffic slice). Run canary for 45 minutes with synthetic probes (latency, token error rate, prefix accuracy).
- If canary fails: immediate auto-abort and rollback via the orchestration controller.

Pinning approach (answers Gloria's ask)
- When we launch, we will set a "soft pin" on platform revision for Acme for 72 hours: this prevents automatic continuous deployment from moving them forward but allows manual roll-forward once telemetry gates are green.
- We will snapshot service binaries + kernel spec and write a version diff to the audit log (immutable record) — will be available to share for SOC2 evidence.

Rollback timeline and mechanics
- Fast rollback target: 3-7 min per pod to rehydrate to previous revision (KV cache conservative TTL + warmup). Full fleet rollback target: under 30 minutes if all opts go well.
- Rollback checklist will include: network path sanity, KMS key verification, endpoint routing check, and post-rollback smoke tests. See attached rollback-checklist.md.

Telemetry & Audit
- We'll export a telemetry snapshot (telemetry-matrix.csv) to the shared Drive folder at t0, t+30m, t+2h, t+24h.
- KMS operations will be logged and we can provide the KMS operation ids for audit.

Notes/risks
- If the reporting job at 04:30 UTC is considered critical, we will avoid draining pods in that AZ during that 45-minute window.
- Network ACL changes are out of scope for this maintenance; any required firewall changes must be scheduled separately.

Attachments: rollback-checklist.md, telemetry-matrix.csv

I'll prepare the canary runbook (canary-runbook.odt) and want to run a dry-run in staging on 11/25.

Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private maintenance safety-lane: confirmation and final runbook

Hi Gloria — thanks for the quick turnaround. Following Monica's notes, here's the consolidated plan and acceptance items we need from Acme:

Final schedule
- Start: 2026-11-27 02:00 UTC
- End: 2026-11-27 06:00 UTC
- Canary staging dry-run: 2026-11-25 10:00 UTC (recommended)

Operational constraints handled
- We'll avoid draining pods in the AZ that runs your 04:30 reporting job during 04:00-05:30 UTC. Canary and patching will target other AZ slices first, then the non-critical AZ slice during the job quiet period.

Pinning & telemetry
- Soft pin for 72 hours as Monica outlined. Pin can be manually extended by Acme if you request it via support ticket.
- We will publish the audit diff and KMS operation ids into the shared Drive folder. SOC 2 control map (redacted where needed) will be attached to the drive link.

Rollback criteria (short form)
- Abort if token error rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes on canary
- Abort if median generation latency increases > 40%
- Manual abort triggers: customer-reported severity P1 or security anomaly

Acceptance checklist for Acme (please confirm):
- [ ] Approve the 11/27 02:00-06:00 UTC window
- [ ] Confirm we may avoid the reporting AZ between 04:00-05:30 UTC as planned
- [ ] Confirm who should receive the KMS operation audit artifacts (email addresses)

Attachments: canary-runbook.odt, maintenance-plan-outline.pdf
Related links: JIRA SUP-9234, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-maintenance-docs

If all good, I'll schedule the dry-run and send an updated runbook + Cal invite.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
